clue.text: Artist coming in accompanied by ill-looking person

indicators.note: coming in says the artist enters the other word and sits inside it

parts.note: accompanied by means together with
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist

explanation.surface: A painter turns up in the company of someone who looks unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: RA goes into WITH to make WRAITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or a pale, gaunt figure, so the word describes someone looking deathly ill.

clue.text: Liquid running short around South — leakage?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shortened word encloses the extra letter
running short means falling a little short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: water is the liquid of choice
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A plumber suspects a leak because the water supply around the south side keeps running low.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that leakage is only one example of waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is a form of waste, resources lost to no purpose, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Drunken lout had excessive drugs? That's maturity?

indicators.note: drunken means staggering about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
OD is an overdose, an excess of drugs

explanation.surface: A drunk yob who has taken too much asks sarcastically whether this is growing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulthood is the state of being fully grown, the stage of life when one is mature.

clue.text: Attempt to suppress historic disaster

indicators.note: to suppress means to hold down and keep in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means old, historic

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hush up a catastrophe from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a dreadful event causing great suffering, a calamity.

clue.text: Bad response: Liberal remains chasing support

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so these pieces come after the word for support

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A political commentator reports a poor reaction as Liberal remnants trail behind their backers.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong hostile reaction against some change or event, a negative public reply.

clue.text: Relative looking haggard? Not good

indicators.note: not good means the letter standing for good, G, is taken away

parts.note: gaunt means looking haggard and thin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a family member looking worn out is a bad sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family member, a parent's sister or an uncle's wife.

clue.text: Pay for ongoing promotion, having received new support

indicators.note: having received means taking something in, so the first word holds the extra letter

parts.note: to keep someone is to pay for their continuing upkeep
N is the abbreviation for new
an ad, an advertisement, is a promotion

explanation.surface: A firm funds a continuing marketing campaign once fresh sponsorship arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneepad is protective padding worn over the knee, a form of support for the joint.

clue.text: Unwell — a third reduced — after consuming old garlic dressing

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the shortened word takes another letter inside
a third reduced means a third of the word's letters are cut away

parts.note: ailing means unwell
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone sick after eating a stale garlic sauce has lost a third of their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Six letters lose two, the final third, before the O goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal sauce of garlic and olive oil, a mayonnaise served as a dressing or dip.

clue.text: That chap's simple and cruel

parts.note: he is that chap
artless means simple, without guile

explanation.surface: A description of a man who is both naive and unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartless means lacking compassion, cold and unfeeling towards others' suffering.

clue.text: An American recalled consuming a Finnish speciality

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the words are read from the end backwards
consuming means swallowing, so the reversed letters hold another piece inside

parts.note: An taken as written, plus US for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American remembers eating a famous dish from Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: AN US runs backwards to SUNA, which takes in A after its second letter to make SAUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The sauna, a hot steam room for bathing, is the best-known cultural institution of Finland.

clue.text: US state released no inmates

indicators.note: released means set loose, so the letters are freed to fall into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item: an American state's prisons have let all their prisoners go.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty states of America, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: My lecture, cut short, interrupted by drunken noise of legendary stature

indicators.note: interrupted by means something breaks into the middle of the shortened word
cut short means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: taken as written
a talk is a lecture
hic is the sound of a drunk's hiccup

explanation.surface: A speaker complains that their lecture was cut off by a drunk's hiccups, a legendary event.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical means existing in myth or legend, so it describes something of legendary status.

clue.text: Request access to bring in a lot of food

indicators.note: to bring in means the first word takes the shortened word inside it

parts.note: entry is a way in, access

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission to carry plenty of food into a place.
explanation.walkthrough: Eats is informal British for food; 'a lot of' leaves all but its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal, a request made with feeling.

clue.text: Put out about curtailment of long sentence offering enlightenment

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the shortened word
out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term

explanation.surface: A prisoner, annoyed that a long sentence has been cut, nonetheless finds it brings insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long sentence' looks like grammar, but it is a prison term for life.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplift is moral or spiritual elevation, the raising of the mind that enlightenment also brings.

clue.text: After ingesting cocaine, favoured examination of the chest

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the next word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: pet as an adjective means favourite
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: After taking drugs, someone goes for a preferred check-up of their chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectoral is the anatomical adjective relating to the chest or breast, as in pectoral muscles.

clue.text: Singular right-wing policy narrative

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a Tory is a member of Britain's right-of-centre Conservative Party
the party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A commentator describes an unusual conservative policy as a story the party tells.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the plot of a novel, play or film, its narrative thread.

clue.text: Murderer with change of heart? One wanders all over the place

definitions.text: One wanders all over the place

indicators.note: change of heart means the middle letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a strangler is a killer who throttles victims

explanation.surface: A killer has a moral change of heart and drifts aimlessly afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The central N becomes G; 'change of heart' sounds moral but is literal surgery on the middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler is someone who strays from the group or lags behind, wandering apart.

clue.text: Divine party? Sensible to abandon one

indicators.note: to abandon one tells us the letter standing for one, I, is dropped

parts.note: a do is a party
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a heavenly party is a good idea, then thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective about heaven; it is the verb, to search for water with a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water or metal with a rod, which is also called divining.

clue.text: Wisecrack? Habitual response is following it in West Midlands at first

indicators.note: in places the whole sequence inside the two initial letters
following means coming after, so these pieces go after the word it
at first means take only the opening letters of the place name

parts.note: the first letter of West
taken as written
a tic is an habitual involuntary twitch
taken as written
the first letter of Midlands

explanation.surface: A joke about someone whose reflexive reaction in Birmingham is to follow along.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Midlands is an English region around Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A witticism is a clever, witty remark, essentially a wisecrack; the question mark marks the loose match.

clue.text: Trips I had, interrupting a lot of relaxation

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the shortened word
a lot of, but not all, means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rest is relaxation
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls journeys that broke up a long holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Rides are journeys on a vehicle or animal, short trips out.

clue.text: Small and reduced amount of light about a disgraceful act

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the next piece
reduced means made shorter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the candle is an old unit of luminous intensity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dim, small light hangs over some shameful deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an action or event causing public outrage, a shameful affair.

clue.text: Inflammation? Skill is to limit brief time with it

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose with boundaries, so the outer words go around the rest

parts.note: art is skill
taken as written
HR is the short form of hour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sufferer asks whether swelling is the price of cramming craft into a short period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skill is' stays together as the outer frame, split around the middle pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is painful inflammation of the joints, so it is a specific kind of inflammation.

clue.text: Bleed, part of leg cut at top — seem likely to overflow?

indicators.note: cut at top means the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: dye or colours run, that is bleed
the thigh is the upper part of the leg

explanation.surface: A wound in the upper leg bleeds so badly it threatens to spill over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers and emotions run high when they are swollen or intense, close to brimming over.

clue.text: American dietitian reduced interest associated with meat

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to grab someone is to interest them, as in 'how does that grab you?'
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A diet expert from the US links lower interest in eating to meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sylvester Graham was a 19th-century American diet reformer, remembered in the graham cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester Graham was a nineteenth-century American preacher who championed vegetarian eating and wholemeal flour.

clue.text: A black stain seeing removal of second religious leader

indicators.note: removal of second means the second letter of that word is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a blot is a stain

explanation.surface: A dark mark is removed from a clergyman's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of a monastery, a senior figure in a religious order.

clue.text: Wild din swamped by forward flourish

indicators.note: swamped by means engulfed, so the rearranged letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: brash means pushy, forward

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A loud racket is drowned out by a bold flourish of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' reads like a noun after the music, but the definition is the verb, to wave about.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to wave or flourish it about showily.

clue.text: Chairperson losing time touring Middle Eastern houses

losing time means the letter standing for time, T, is dropped

parts.note: the host of a show chairs it
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East

explanation.surface: A busy chairman on a whistle-stop trip round the Middle East views properties.
explanation.definitionFit: Homes are dwellings where people live, so the plural noun matches houses.

clue.text: Responsibility sees our team supporting cricket side

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath, so this piece goes below

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
us is our own team

explanation.surface: A captain feels the burden of his own team backing a cricket eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket side' looks like a team; it is half of the field, the on or leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is a duty or burden, the obligation to do something, as in the onus of proof.

clue.text: Liberation in two-thirds of ladies possibly linked to sexual urge

parts.note: Lib is the short form of liberation, as in Women's Lib

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, not the given one
two-thirds of means only four of the six letters are kept, the end two cut

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
only its first four letters are used in the anagram

clue.text: I turn down accepting ordinary way of speaking

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression or a characteristic manner of expression in a language.

clue.text: Routine line adopted by British pianist without consideration

explanation.definitionFit: Rhymes are short poems or lines of verse, as in nursery rhymes.
